# moddotplot-rs design reference

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

This is the authoritative engineering design. The narrower
[scientific specification](SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md) is normative for numeric behavior;
[ADR 0004](adr/0004-validated-production-backend.md) records how the current backend
was selected.

## 1. Product requirements

moddotplot-rs is a static, install-free desktop web application for interactive self
and pairwise genomic dotplots.

Required behavior:

1. Load one or more FASTA records locally, with a one-billion-base record bound.
2. Select any record independently for each axis; self comparison is not a separate
   scientific code path.
3. Show a recognizable overview as early as possible, then improve it without blocking
   pan or zoom.
4. Preserve ModDotPlot maximum-containment semantics and display `ANI_c=C^(1/k)`,
   without treating `ANI_c` as biological average nucleotide identity.
5. Distinguish forward and reverse matches with evidence-aware color confidence.
6. Generate higher-resolution matrix tiles on demand, cache reusable work, prefetch a
   one-tile halo, and reach exact k-mer resolution.
7. Keep sequence data inside the browser and make method provenance
   available for reproducible figures.
8. Prefer scientific correctness over throughput, then optimize within the validated
   estimator contract.

No mobile support or session persistence is required in the current scope. Numeric
tiles are deliberately renderer-independent; export does not change the estimator.

## 2. System architecture

```text
FASTA File streams
      │
      ▼
compute Web Worker ── Wasm ComputeSession ── PackedSequence
      │                      │
      │                      ├─ BuildSketch (temporary full OPH/HLL)
      │                      ├─ FrozenAxis (retained bit planes/scalars)
      │                      └─ bounded zoom-axis cache
      │
      ├─ transferable numeric MatrixTile channels
      ▼
main thread ── immutable renderer tile cache ── WebGL2 canvas
      │
      ├─ viewport/axes/controls/provenance
      └─ BEDPE/CSV and full-composition PNG/SVG/PDF export
```

The main thread owns interaction and rendering only. FASTA parsing, sketch construction,
matrix comparison, and gzip decompression run in a worker. The site has
no runtime API, CDN dependency, telemetry, or analytics.

### Core crate

`moddotplot-core` is browser-independent and dependency-free. Its maintained surface is:

* packed DNA and streaming FASTA parsing;
* canonical ntHash2;
* undensified OPH and HLL;
* compact bit-sliced signatures and containment conversion;
* exact canonical k-mer sets used only as the scientific oracle;
* exact terminal k-mer tiles;
* axis construction, frozen summaries, and numeric tiles;
* immutable validated scientific configuration.

Rejected production candidates are not used by the browser. Git tag `v0.1.0` preserves
the old Phase 0/minmer/MashMap-compatible code when historical inspection is needed.
Candidate estimators, fused projection, sparse policy, and sparse kernels remain
available only through the non-default Rust `validation` module. The browser
distribution does not compile that feature or expose sparse correction.

### Wasm crate

`moddotplot-wasm` exposes a narrow stateful API:

* incremental FASTA transactions;
* scientific configuration metadata and digest;
* chunked, cancellable overview preparation;
* overview, zoom, and terminal tile requests;
* resource admission and memory estimates;
* consuming tile-channel transfer methods.

Preparation, exact cache identity, resource admission, composition state, and immutable
session selection context have separate ownership modules behind the thin binding.
It owns sequences and scientific caches. JavaScript never receives raw sequence bytes
except short base-code spans needed for exact terminal coloring.

### Browser application

The compute worker serializes state mutations and transfers owned typed arrays. Loaded
datasets, comparisons, and feature-track requests have separate immutable job IDs,
cancellation signals, configuration ownership, and publication guards. The renderer
retains CPU arrays for hover, context restoration, and cache fallback, plus one GPU
texture per tile channel.

## 3. Data representations

### PackedSequence

Two bits store each base and a sparse invalid-base bit vector distinguishes `A/C/G/T/U` from ambiguity
or gaps. `U/u` is normalized to `T/t`. Coordinates remain `u64`; no normalization may
shift them. FASTA is parsed incrementally and records are committed transactionally.

### BuildSketch and FrozenAxis

An `OphSketch` temporarily stores full 64-bit winners, orientation, HLL, and observation
count. Axis construction hashes each relevant k-mer once into half-bin sketches, then
merges exact register winners into core and expanded cells.

Each axis also owns the complete validated `ScientificConfig` and source-sequence
identity. `FrozenAxis` storage is private; ordinary `TileRequest` values are geometric
only, and tile parameters are derived from compatible axes before allocation.

`AxisOverview::freeze` discards builders and retains only:

* coordinate bounds and sequence metadata;
* register occupancy;
* 32 fingerprint bit planes;
* reverse and ambiguous orientation planes;
* HLL cardinality and observation scalars;
* optional complete sparse-core hash sets.

This prevents the previous double retention of full winners plus bit planes.

### MatrixTile

Tiles are row-major arrays with equal dimensions:

* `Uint16 identity`, scaled by 10,000; `65535` is missing;
* `Int16 direction`, scaled to `[-32767,32767]`;
* `Uint16 directionSupport`.

Wasm consumes its Rust vectors when returning channels. wasm-bindgen performs the one
necessary Wasm-to-JavaScript copy, after which the worker transfers ownership to the
main thread without another `.slice()`.

## 4. Scientific pipeline

The complete estimator is specified in [SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md](SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md).
Important implementation properties are:

* matched verified OPH winners divided by union-occupied registers estimates Jaccard;
* 14 low planes prefilter candidate equality, while 32 planes verify the statistic;
* HLL p10 provides cardinality at lower memory than the original p12 candidate;
* both directed containment estimates contribute orientation evidence;
* only the larger directed containment controls displayed identity;
* exact canonical k-mer sets, not production hashes or another estimator, are the
  validation oracle.

The default 85% palette floor is a display decision. The numerical tile retains values
below it, allowing immediate recoloring down to the advanced 80% limit.

## 5. Progressive scheduling

### Overview

1. Stream and pack FASTA.
2. Build 256-register axes in aligned 256-cell chunks with visible progress.
3. As soon as compatible chunks exist, compute and transfer their quick matrix block.
   Self comparisons expose diagonal and completed off-diagonal blocks incrementally;
   pairwise comparisons expose blocks as each Y chunk joins the completed X chunks.
4. Wait for the renderer's `preview-presented` acknowledgement.
5. Build the 1,024-register detailed axes in aligned chunks and transfer each selected
   detailed block as soon as compatible X/Y chunks exist.
6. Refine tiles whose preview is uncertain around the active display floor or has low
   support, their immediate neighbors, and a deterministic exploratory sample, in
   descending priority order.

Scheduler policy 2 stores 101-bin identity and low-support histograms for each preview
tile before its transferable channels leave the worker. The current palette minimum,
plus or minus five percentage points, defines the active decision region. Immediate
neighbors preserve coherent structure, while a deterministic one-in-sixteen tile
sample prevents a blank preview region from becoming a permanent exclusion rule.
Changing the palette floor updates future selection without recomputing numeric tiles.

Uncertainty is only a display scheduling heuristic. It selects which provisional tiles
receive the detailed estimator and never changes either estimator's numeric result.

### Why quick and detailed builds remain separate

A fine OPH sketch can be projected exactly into a coarser partition. A release-mode
8 Mb/1,000-cell benchmark measured 591 ms for a 2,048-register build plus projection,
versus 672 ms for separate 256 and 2,048 builds. However, projected first paint waited
533 ms instead of 139 ms. The 12% final-time saving did not justify a 3.8-fold first-view
delay, so the interactive path remains quick-first. Projection code and the ignored
benchmark are retained to detect future crossover changes.

### Navigation

The renderer immediately transforms existing lower-resolution tiles during zoom so the
canvas never flashes white. The main thread selects visible 256-cell tiles plus a
one-tile halo. A new request id cancels stale detailed work. Quick tiles for the new
viewport arrive first; detailed refinement begins only after paint acknowledgement.
Exact terminal tiles replace sketches at one base pair per matrix position and extend
each matching k-mer across its complete footprint.

## 6. State and cancellation

The compute worker uses a serialized promise queue plus owned `DatasetSession`,
`ComparisonJob`, and `FeatureJob` lifetimes. A dataset can serve several later
comparison generations, while each comparison and feature publication must match its
own current immutable identity.

```text
Empty → Loading(staging session) → Ready(committed dataset)
                          │
                          └─ newer load/clear discards staging

Ready → Preparing(request/config) → Serving(preview) → Serving(refined)
                   │                         │
                   └──── newer request cancels stale publication ────┘
```

Load is transactional: files are read into a staging `ComputeSession`; the committed
session changes only after every record succeeds and the operation is still current.
Every dataset-dependent worker message carries a generation. Every tile additionally
carries quality, resolution, coordinates, and configuration digest. The main thread
rejects stale generations even if a browser delivers messages late.

`preview-presented` and cancellation messages bypass queued heavy work so they can take
effect at yield boundaries. Preparation, tile, and annotation-stream loops yield at
bounded shards. Cancelled jobs cannot publish terminal data.

## 7. Cache and memory policy

Memory admission happens before large allocations.

* Wasm zoom-axis cache: 192 MiB.
* Prepared frozen axes: 384 MiB.
* Application-owned Wasm session budget: 3 GiB.
* JavaScript tile cache: 96 MiB.
* GPU textures: 96 MiB.
* Imported annotations: 512 MiB.
* Computed feature tracks: 64 MiB.
* Transient publication: 256 MiB.
* Complete cross-layer plan: 4 GiB.

The Wasm axis cache uses a recency map with logarithmic touch/eviction and tracks
estimated heap bytes. Renderer tile keys include resolution, coordinates, and the
complete configuration digest; quality ranks replacement when a key is shared, and
incompatible tiles cannot alias. Eviction is coordinated back to
the worker so its published-tile bookkeeping cannot grow without bound. The current
overview plus tiles required to avoid a blank viewport are protected, so an unusually
large active viewport can temporarily exceed the renderer's nominal cache budget.

Before risky allocation, the applicable plan selects admission, cache eviction,
quality downgrade, bounded sharding, or rejection with a user-facing fallback. OPFS
spill is reserved but disabled until measurements justify its browser complexity.
Reported memory includes packed sequences, retained Wasm structures, tile CPU arrays,
estimated textures, annotations, and feature tracks. It excludes allocator metadata,
browser internals, and driver overhead. Wasm linear memory can reuse freed regions but
normally does not shrink; reloading the page resets the instance.

## 8. Rendering and recovery

WebGL2 shaders apply the similarity or direction palette without changing numeric
tiles. Similarity uses the selected plot background below the minimum, maps the chosen
palette linearly across the minimum/midpoint and midpoint/maximum segments, and retains
the palette's top color above the maximum. Direction uses separate forward/reverse hues
blended toward equal-luminance gray at low support.

On `webglcontextlost`, rendering pauses and default loss handling is prevented. On
restore, the program, uniforms, geometry, fallback texture, and every GPU tile texture
are reconstructed from retained CPU arrays. Keyboard controls provide arrow-key pan,
`+/-` zoom, and `Home` reset. The canvas remains focusable and labeled.

Numeric export writes current-view renderer cells as BEDPE by default or complete
fixed-point CSV. Construction is rejected above two million participating cells.
Image export includes the heatmap, axes, sequence labels, and visible tracks as PNG,
SVG, or PDF. SVG/PDF embed the heatmap as raster while keeping the other components
vectorized. All formats carry complete software, method, scheduler, comparison,
scientific-configuration, display, viewport, and sequence provenance.

## 9. Security and privacy

The application processes user files locally. A restrictive CSP permits same-origin
scripts/assets, Wasm evaluation, same-origin/blob workers, data images, and local Vite
WebSockets during development; objects and base-URI changes are forbidden. Deployment
must send an equivalent or stricter HTTP header. Automated browser tests fail on
unexpected network egress while processing a fixture.

## 10. Verification pyramid

| Layer | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Unit | Parsing, normalization, coordinates, hashing vectors, set operations, UI math |
| Kernel differential | Bit-sliced OPH counters versus test-only scalar comparison |
| Scientific differential | Production score versus exact distinct canonical k-mer containment |
| Statistical/spatial | Multi-realization error, bias, threshold confusion, holes, isolated pixels, continuity, fingerprint events |
| Wasm/browser | Real build, load cancellation, exact entry, transfer semantics, progressive refinement, worker/context recovery, privacy, keyboard |
| Release | Pinned tools/actions, atomic build, SBOM/licenses, separate artifacts, checksums, provenance, biological timing |

Normal CI keeps exact fixtures small and bounded. Chromosome-scale runs measure time and
memory without attempting an exact all-pairs oracle.

## 11. Extension points

### Export

The v0.5 export represents the current viewport and its current mix of preview,
refined, and exact renderer inputs. A future explicit publication tier may request and
freeze an all-detailed viewport before export; that would be a usability feature, not a
change to the current scientific configuration.

### Persistence and 1 Gb operation

Current state is session-local. Robust one-billion-base operation may require sharded
packed sequences, bounded OPFS spill, and a user-visible storage policy. Any persistence
must be opt-in, origin-scoped, versioned, and clearable; it must not weaken the local-only
privacy contract.
